name: Buchla 291-style morphing bandpass: 6-pole bandpass with two clocked step sequencers (frequency and bandwidth) as filter snapshots, wet/dry crossfader
goal: Build a free West-Coast-style morphing filter: a steep 6-pole bandpass (bandwidth instead of resonance) fed a harmonically rich complex oscillator, with two clocked, randomized 8-step sequencers — one on frequency (v/oct, ±10 V) and one on bandwidth (0–10 V) — so each clock step jumps to a new 'filter snapshot', blended with the dry signal on a crossfader like an aux, plus optional LFO on the main frequency; copy the voice for a triple morphing filter.

source.title: How to make your own Buchla Style Morphing Filter in VCV

prerequisites: Multimode filter with selectable slope (6-pole) and bandpass bandwidth control (Web Audio: cascade 3 bandpass BiquadFilterNodes, implementation note)
Two step sequencers with settable output ranges, a clock

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Complex/harmonically rich oscillator (a plain sine disappears in a bandpass)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Pure sine sources vanish through a narrow bandpass — make the source complex/brighter first.
Sequencer ranges matter: frequency bipolar ±10 V, bandwidth unipolar 0–10 V (scale to Hz/Q in other environments).
FM/AM/ring-mod inputs of the hardware 291e are not reproduced here; only one mode at a time in this build.

steps.action: Choose a multimode filter, set it to bandpass and the slope to 6 poles (type the value precisely); set bandwidth to 100%.
Feed a complex oscillator; brighten/complexify it and raise the pitch until the bandpass has harmonics to work with. Sweep bandwidth to hear the change.
Add two step sequencers: one to filter frequency (v/oct), output range ±10 V; one to bandwidth, range 0–10 V.
Put a crossfader after the filter: filtered signal on A, dry signal on B, so the filter acts like an aux/wet-dry morph.
Clock both sequencers, randomize all steps, set 8 steps forward, and run: each step recalls a different frequency+bandwidth 'snapshot'.
steps.expect: Rhythmic jumps between distinct filter snapshots

steps.action: Adjust main frequency/bandwidth controls live and optionally modulate main frequency with an LFO via CV.
steps.expect: Further variety on top of the stepped snapshots

steps.action: For a triple morphing filter, duplicate the whole voice (filter + two sequencers) and offset settings.

verification: Each clock step audibly changes both centre frequency and bandwidth.
Crossfader at B gives the dry source; at A the full filtered sound.
With a pure sine source the effect is weak — confirming the need for a rich source.
